previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, tracheostomy, and a history of recurrent infections was admitted with altered mental status and respiratory failure. He was found to have multifocal pneumonia due to Serratia and Proteus, requiring intubation and ventilator support, and a vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus urinary tract infection. He was treated with cefepime for pneumonia and linezolid for the UTI, with successful weaning from the ventilator. His altered mental status, attributed to toxic metabolic encephalopathy, resolved with treatment. The citalopram dose was temporarily reduced due to interaction risk with linezolid. He was discharged to extended care on day 7 to complete his antibiotic courses, with glycopyrrolate added to manage secretions.
problems: Pneumonia due to other Gram-negative bacteria
Acute and chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with PICC placed at OSH// PICC location

IMPRESSION: 

In comparison with study ___, there is a right subclavian PICC line in
place that extends to the lower SVC.  Continued diffuse bilateral pulmonary
interstitial opacities with tracheostomy tube in place.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with G-J tube, transfer from ___ for clogged
J limb// exchange

COMPARISON:  Percutaneous GJ tube check ___

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ and Dr.
___ radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
supervised the trainee during the key components of the procedure and has
reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
25 mcg of fentanyl and 0 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of  during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse.
MEDICATIONS: None.
CONTRAST: 20 ml of Optiray
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 1 min, 14 mGy

PROCEDURE:  Low profile MIC gastrojejunostomy exchange.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The tube site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

The existing tube was injected with contrast and showed opacification of the
gastric rugae and duodenum.  An Amplatz wire was introduced into the jejunum.
The existing feeding tube was then removed. An ___ F sheath 3.5 cm stomal
length 45 cm low profile MIC gastrojejunostomy catheter was advanced over the
wire into position.  The balloon was inflated with 8 cc of dilute contrast. 
The wire was then removed. Contrast was injected to confirm Catheter position
within the jejunum.

The catheter was then flushed. Sterile dressings were applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

1.  Appropriately positioned new 18 ___ low profile 3.5 cm stoma length MIC
gastrojejunostomy tube.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful exchange of a gastrojejunostomy tube for a new 18 ___ low
profile 3.5 cm stoma length MIC gastrojejunostomy tube. The tube is ready to
use.
